name: ai.bithuman/characters
title: bitHuman
description: Animated AI characters in your chat: short clips of a character saying your words, or a live talk.

tools.name: list_characters
tools.description: List the bitHuman house characters that can speak. Each has an id (pass it as `character` to make_character_video or talk_to_character), a name, a short description, a picture URL and `talk` (true when talk_to_character is open for it). No arguments and read-only; one call per conversation is enough. Only these characters can speak: real people, photos and custom voices are not supported.

tools.name: make_character_video
tools.description: Make a short video of one bitHuman house character saying `text` word for word, in its own voice. Returns video_url (an MP4 that plays inline and expires after 7 days), duration_seconds and share_url, labelled AI character. Example: {"character": "wise-pup", "text": "Welcome back! Ready for today's lesson?"}. Limits: `text` is 3 to 200 characters and at most 19 seconds when spoken (about 15 s is typical); one video at a time per user; 10 videos per user per UTC day; the same character and text again replays the earlier clip at once. Errors come back as isError with one sentence saying what to do: an unknown character (call list_characters), text too short or too long (rewrite it), personal information such as a phone number, email or street address (remove it), busy (retry in a minute), the daily limit (try again after 00:00 UTC), resting (try later). To hold a conversation in character, write each reply yourself and call this tool once per reply.

text.description: The exact words the character says, 3 to 200 characters (at most 19 seconds of speech). No personal information.

tools.name: talk_to_character
tools.description: Open a live voice conversation with one bitHuman house character in a player in the chat. The user presses Start and speaks through the microphone; the character answers out loud. A conversation lasts up to 60 seconds (max_seconds), then ends by itself; call again for another. Returns session_url: when the host shows no player, give the user that link. Example: {"character": "wise-pup"}. Needs a microphone in the user's browser. Errors come back as isError: an unknown character (call list_characters and use an id whose `talk` is true), resting (live conversations are off right now; make_character_video still works).
